_comment: The one OpenShell release this branch is built on (ADR 0009). Read by the
compat job in ci.yml, by the Follow upstream workflow, by
deploy/ci/e2e-stack.sh and by scripts/gateway-range.mjs.
release: the upstream release, without the leading v. Everything that
comes from it is below and moves with it, in one commit. The gateway
release line this build is for is its major.minor; that line is also
compiled into the BFF, and `node scripts/gateway-range.mjs --check` fails
when the two disagree. On `main` and `release/**` this is a stable
release, X.Y.Z. Only `next` pins a pre-release, X.Y.Z-pre.N, and CI
refuses one in a pull request into any other branch.
sdk: the exact version required in backend/go.mod: the SDK at the commit
upstream tagged this release with. CI fails when the two disagree.
gateway_image, supervisor_image: that release's images, pinned by digest
(tag@digest: the tag is for readers, the digest is what gets pulled).
Never a dev build: a dev gateway resolves
ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/sandbox:dev at runtime, so even pinned by digest
it drifts with upstream HEAD, which broke main on 2026-10-02.
sandbox_image: the workload image compat sandboxes run. It publishes no
version tags, so it is pinned by digest and does not move with the
release.
config_schema: which deploy/ci/gateway.e2e.<schema>.toml.tmpl this
gateway's config is rendered from.
Nobody edits this by hand to follow upstream. The Follow upstream
workflow finds new releases from upstream's tags and moves all of it on
the `next` branch (deploy/ci/upstream/README.md). It rewrites the whole
file, so CI requires the exact form it writes: after a hand edit, run
`python3 deploy/ci/upstream/follow.py format-pins`.
